newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish money market cash-heavy despite drainage.
newsitem.headline: Polish money market cash-heavy despite drainage.

text.p: Polish money market remained overliquid despite today's National Bank of Poland's 2.15 billion zloty one-day reverse repo, at which the central bank slashed its maximum accepted rate from its last drainage.
The central bank set the maximum accepted rate at 15.90 percent, down from Friday's 17.70 percent for a three-day operation and its last 14-day drainage rate of 19.12 percent.
"The market is flooded with cash and players are trying to place it anywhere they can -- so rates are falling," said Radek Radziszewski, deputy chief dealer at Pekao SA.

Despite today's drainage, which attracted 2.93 billion zlotys worth of bids, tomorrow/next rates eased to close at 11.0/14.0 percent from 14.0/16.5 percent in early trade and overnight deposits closed at 10.0/12.0 percent from 8.0/12.0.

Dealers said the NBP's policy, which concentrates on controlling reserve money levels and not short-term rate swings, led to overliquidity on the money market in August due to seasonal money supply swings caused by holiday-makers.
"The NBP is keeping the market flooded with cash and rates are falling because the central bank is primarly concerned with reserve money levels," said Marek Zielnski of Bank Slaski SA.
Dealers said the money market was likely to remain cash-heavy for the rest of this week because more money was due to return from reverse-repo buy back during the next few days.
The overliquity stirred up 3.1 billion zlotys worth of demand at today's 600 million zloty primary T-bill tender and depressed yields further than analysts expected.
The benchmark 52-week average yield fell to 19.46 percent from last week's 19.73 percent and analyst expectations of around 19.6 percent.
The average 26-week bill yield fell to 19.35 percent from 19.68 and the 8-week paper to 18.65 percent from 19.06.
The 13-week T-bill average yield was slashed to 18.94 percent, down from 19.51 percent on August 8 -- the last primary auction that the bill was offered.
The zloty drifted sideways for most of the slow session after inching up at the opening to close at 1.80/1.75 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's 1.75/1.70.
It was at 2.7310/20 per dollar, up from 2.7405/25 on Friday, and at 1.8470/80 to the mark, down from 1.8423/28.
